Video: UDA MP ranks opposition leaders, names one he considers most suitable
items.description: The outspoken UDA MP listed the strengths and weaknesses of opposition leaders and named one he considers to be the most suitable to run as a presidential candidate.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!

Molo Member of Parliament Kuria Kimani, who also chairs the National Assembly's Budget Committee and serves as a United Democratic Alliance (UDA) member, has publicly ranked key opposition figures on their suitability for the presidency, singling out Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka as the most relatable candidate among the current crop of contenders.

Speaking in an interview with Obinna, Kimani described Kalonzo as experienced, diplomatic, and notably non-confrontational, qualities he said would make it easier for ordinary Kenyans to accept him as a national leader.

The MP was more sceptical about former Interior Cabinet Secretary Fred Matiang'i, arguing that he has no meaningful electoral experience and would struggle to mobilise grassroots support.

Kimani challenged whether Matiang'i could even name a thousand people he knows personally across the country, saying that precise, name-by-name voter mobilisation is a core skill in Kenyan politics, one he said Matiang'i has never had to develop independently because the state machinery did it for him during his time in government.
On Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM) leader Edwin Sifuna , Kimani acknowledged that he has some practical experience of running a campaign, calling it a foundation others in the opposition lack.
Sifuna is currently in the United States to meet and rally Kenyans in the diaspora behind him in the upcoming General Election.
Fred Matiang’i names opposition leaders he cannot work with as cracks deepen
Regarding former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua , Kimani acknowledged his strength as a mobiliser but pointed to what he described as a critical and self-inflicted setback.

"If you take Rigathi Gachagua, good mobiliser, but he made one mistake. He allowed himself to be impeached. And therefore in our constitution, if you are impeached, you can never run for office," Kimani said.
Gachagua was impeached by Parliament in October 2024, a move he has since contested through the courts.

When asked directly whether the 2027 election is already settled, Kimani was blunt, suggesting that any serious presidential aspirant should shift their focus to 2032, a clear signal of his confidence that President William Ruto will secure a second term.

Sifuna in Maryland: 'Ruto Has No Path to Power as United Opposition Eyes 80% Vote'
items.description: Nairobi Senator Edwin Watenya Sifuna addressed Kenyans living in Maryland during his United States diaspora tour, detailing his reluctant role in drafting th...
content: Nairobi Senator Edwin Watenya Sifuna addressed Kenyans living in Maryland during his United States diaspora tour, detailing his reluctant role in drafting the p...

Nairobi Senator Edwin Watenya Sifuna addressed Kenyans living in Maryland during his United States diaspora tour, detailing his reluctant role in drafting the previous political agreement with the United Democratic Alliance (UDA). He noted that the pact was originally designed to stabilize the nation and protect human life amid widespread street demonstrations.
"I was the person, unfortunately, who was charged with drafting this agreement that was going to govern this relationship, and I feel that I stayed true to what I believe in," Sifuna said.

According to Sifuna, the agreement contained two non-negotiable pillars: an immediate halt to extrajudicial killings and abductions of youth, and an independent inquiry into the June 2024 protests. He emphasized that the pact explicitly required holding culpable police officers accountable under Kenyan law.

"I wrote into that agreement that we were no longer going to experience abductions and killings of young people. We were going to have an independent review of the happenings of June 2024, that police officers who are responsible for the killings of young people would be held to account in accordance with our laws," he explained.

Sifuna revealed that he publicly declared the agreement dead on television following the death of a young man, Albert Ojwang (referenced in the transcript as Albert/Alberto Jang), who was transported over 400 kilometers to Nairobi and died in police custody. The senator argued that the arrangement lost all value once the state failed to uphold the sanctity of life.
"If we were going to sustain the democratic state, we needed to sustain life, and there was no compromise about that on the day that they killed Albert," Sifuna stated.

Addressing his political split, Sifuna stated that tensions began when certain colleagues misinterpreted the UDA engagement as an opportunity to access state perks and enrich themselves. He maintained that he rejected efforts to fully back President William Ruto's re-election bid, as it was never part of their original understanding.

"There are people who mistook whatever agreement we had with UDA, and they thought it was time for us to get involvement and get comfortable and gorge ourselves on public resources and so on and so forth. I was not of that thinking," he noted.

Responding to critics urging him to soften his tone ahead of the 2027 general election, Sifuna firmly rejected altering his assertive character to appease voters. He argued that staying silent in the face of falsehoods violates his personal principles and party obligations.
"I have honestly before God, I have never been a nice person. I have never been a person to keep quiet when I feel that something is wrong," Sifuna declared.

Sifuna pointed out that the constitution of the Linda Movement mirrors that of the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM), explicitly obligating party leaders to actively counter misinformation. He insisted that transparency and direct confrontation of lies remain central to his leadership style.
"I have never been a person to play games. I don't have cards that I hide under the table. What you see is what you get, and we will engage you," he said.

During the Maryland forum, Sifuna outlined the vision behind the newly established Linda Mwananchi Movement, describing it as a vehicle to steer Kenya away from its current trajectory. He cited assessments from global financial institutions like the World Bank to argue that weak rule of law and democratic backsliding are stifling national progress.

"So we have managed to put together this new movement, the Linda Movement, and we are hoping that we can build it into a formidable force for good in the election that is coming up," Sifuna told attendees.

The senator praised the diaspora audience for openly associating with him, contrasting their freedom with the intimidation faced by citizens back home. He recounted an incident at a Kenyan university where panicked administrators barred him from addressing students due to fears of state retaliation.

"In Kenya right now, people are living in fear. You people are some of the bravest Kenyans I've known because you are able to say, 'We want to come to our event, and you can record like you are free, you are okay being seen with me,'" he remarked.

Sifuna anchored the Linda Movement's platform on the six foundational values enshrined in the preamble of Kenya’s constitution: democracy, freedom, rule of law, equality, and social justice. He stressed that all government development initiatives must strictly adhere to these constitutional guarantees.
"Our entire platform as Linda Movement is a return to those six constitutional values in our preamble," Sifuna affirmed.

Turning to economic grievances, Sifuna identified the high cost of food, healthcare, education, fuel, and electricity as the primary burden on Kenyans. Drawing from his tenure on the Senate Energy Committee, he revealed that 51 shillings out of every 100 shillings spent on electricity goes directly toward taxes.
"You buy a unit of electricity, and if you pay 100 shillings, 51 shillings goes to taxes out of 100 shillings you pay for a unit of electricity," he pointed out.

Sifuna accused Kenya Power of abruptly halting itemized mobile billing breakdowns after the Senate began investigating daily charges, fuel levies, and forex adjustments. He traced high energy costs to corruption embedded in Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) signed during the 2009 El Niño period, noting that a Senate bill requiring disclosure of beneficial owners remains stalled in the National Assembly.

"Because we went and looked at the power purchase agreements that were signed during the advent of El Niño in 2009, and I can tell you for a fact that the problem has always been corruption," Sifuna asserted.

Addressing healthcare reforms, Sifuna noted that his own monthly contribution rose from 900 shillings under NHIF to 24,000 shillings under the new Social Health scheme. However, he faulted the administration for measuring success by registration numbers rather than service quality or ending medical fundraising appeals.

"He measured success of SH by how many people have registered, and I told him SH is not a registration bureau. It's a healthcare scheme, it's supposed to be measured by the quality of services people are receiving," he stated.

Highlighting demographic pressures, Sifuna noted that Kenya’s national and county governments collectively employ fewer than one million people out of a population of 55 million. With roughly one million young graduates entering the job market annually, he urged diaspora professionals to help educate the public on how private sector investments create jobs.

"Government cannot employ all of us. The entire complement of people who work in government at both levels—the national government and the county governments—is not more than a million people," he explained.

Using regional competition as an example, Sifuna warned that multinational companies base investment decisions on overhead costs rather than sentiment. He noted that high electricity tariffs, corporate taxes, employee-employer co-pays, the housing levy, and demands for 30% kickbacks on projects drive investors toward neighbors like Ethiopia.

"If Ethiopia is selling them power at 30 shillings—30 times less the cost of electricity in Kenya—they're going to put the plant in Ethiopia. It's not about sentiment. It's about bottom line," Sifuna said.

Comparing Kenya’s governance transitions, Sifuna observed that the election of President Mwai Kibaki in 2002 immediately shifted public expectations and empowered citizens to reject police bribery without needing new laws. Conversely, he warned that electing leaders facing corruption or court convictions sends a subliminal signal that legitimizes theft of public funds.

"It's a message that comes from who you elect. If you elect a kleptocratic leader, a conman, somebody who has been convicted in courts and faces other charges in various courts including international courts, you cannot expect that person... not to steal from you," he warned.

Discussing coalition strategy ahead of the 2027 elections, Sifuna projected that a united opposition could capture between 75% and 80% of the national vote, leaving President Ruto with no viable path to victory. He referenced American election analysts Steve Kornacki and John King to illustrate how a unified front would dominate Kenya’s electoral map.

"We believe that a united opposition puts us overwhelmingly over the top—estimates of anywhere upwards of 75% to 80% of the vote. Simply put, William R by the way has no path to power," Sifuna predicted.

Sifuna disclosed that opposition unity negotiations are anchored on two fundamental questions: why Kenyans want the current administration removed, and what immediate reforms will follow once power changes hands. He reported to the diaspora gathering that opposition leaders have made substantial progress toward reaching consensus on both fronts.
"First, what in your view is the reason Kenyans are saying R must go? Question number one. [Second], is the country that Kenyans want to see immediately he goes," he outlined.

Cautioning his opposition allies against complacency, Sifuna emphasized that Kenyan voters will demand tangible governance changes within three months of a new administration taking office. He criticized extravagant displays of wealth by current officials—such as wearing Rolex watches and using helicopters to transport pets—while ordinary citizens struggle to afford food.
"Even in three months, [if] they don't see any recognizable change in the way the affairs of the country are, they will be back in the street singing 'Saba Saba must go,'" Sifuna cautioned.

Citing Auditor General findings and economic experts, Sifuna claimed that between 500 billion and 1.8 trillion shillings is lost annually to budgeted corruption. He called for a complete national reset across both the executive and parliament, urging Kenyans to abandon the culture of lobbying influential figures for government tenders.

"All of you here must stop making those calls to people in influence to help you with tenders and other things. We must all as Kenyans stop this habit of trying to just get ahead by the money equation," he urged.

Referencing World Bank projections, Sifuna stated that curbing corruption could unlock 8.8 million meaningful jobs for Kenyan youth and propel annual economic growth from a sluggish 4% into double digits of up to 25%. Acknowledging his background as a lawyer rather than an economist, he pledged to restore meritocracy and tap into diaspora expertise to execute the movement's manifesto.
"It's okay for leaders to acknowledge that they don't know everything. I am a lawyer... I am not a finance guru, I am not an economic expert, but there exist this expertise," Sifuna admitted.

In his last remarks, Sifuna dismissed claims that a presidential campaign requires 6 billion shillings, noting that his movement relies on organic support rather than paid crowds or printed merchandise. He appealed to the diaspora for logistical backing, technical expertise, and volunteer polling agents to safeguard the vote.

"The money that we need is just for logistics—for me to be able to be present in order for counties, to pay for fuel, for vehicles, and for people to be able to even just have lunch and leave," Sifuna explained.

Hussein Dado Leads Early Tana River Governor Poll
items.description: A Mizani Africa phone poll puts former governor Hussein Dado at 53% for Tana River's open 2027 seat, though 22.6% of surveyed voters remain undecided.
content: A Mizani Africa phone poll puts former governor Hussein Dado at 53% for Tana River's open 2027 seat, though 22.6% of surveyed voters remain undecided.

Former Tana River County Governor Hussein Dado holds a wide early advantage in the contest for the county's top seat ahead of Kenya's 2027 General Election, according to a Mizani Africa survey released on November 25, 2026.

The poll placed Dado at 53 percent support among respondents asked whom they would back if the election were held today, more than four times the share recorded by second-placed Said Hiribae at 12.9 percent. Still, 22.6 percent of respondents said they remained undecided, leaving a substantial swing bloc unaligned more than 20 months before polling day.

Behind Dado and Hiribae, the remaining field polled in single digits in Mizani Africa's snapshot. Nuh Nassir drew 7.3 percent support, followed by Hero Said at 2.3 percent and Hassan Morowa at 1.9 percent, pointing to heavy early consolidation behind the former county chief alongside deep voter hesitation.

Kenya's county governors are elected by simple plurality under Article 180 of the Constitution, running alongside a nominated deputy governor rather than facing a 50-percent runoff threshold. In Mizani Africa's snapshot, the four trailing contenders combined drew 24.4 percent, meaning Dado's 53 percent score exceeds all named rivals and the 22.6 percent undecided group individually, though coalition realignments and undecided turnout still leave the contest fluid.

Under Article 180(7) of the Constitution of Kenya, county governors are barred from holding office for more than two consecutive terms, turning the 2027 contest into an open succession race whenever a two-term incumbent steps aside. In an open field, early name recognition often favours a former governor such as Dado before party nominations and coalition alignments settle the final ballot.

Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) 2022 county data underline how concentrated Tana River's electorate is compared with larger urban counties. Of Kenya's 22,102,532 registered county voters in 2022, Tana River accounted for 141,096 voters across three constituencies: Garsen with 55,453 (39.3 percent of the county total), Bura with 45,678 (32.4 percent), and Galole with 39,965 (28.3 percent).

Within the six Coast counties, IEBC 2022 records show Tana River holds the second-smallest electorate, trailing Mombasa (641,913), Kilifi (588,602), Kwale (328,253), and Taita Taveta (181,827), and standing ahead of only Lamu (81,453). Because total county registration sits near 141,000 voters, modest shifts in turnout or local endorsements across Garsen, Bura, and Galole can swing final margins faster than in populous coastal cities.

Those constituency weights mean a candidate who wins decisive backing in Garsen and Bura can build a commanding county-wide lead even before Galole breaks. Conversely, with 22.6 percent of polled voters undecided, a coordinated shift across any single constituency or late coalition endorsement could alter the gap markedly once formal campaigns begin.

Mizani Africa conducted fieldwork between November 2 and November 12, 2026, using mobile telephone interviews carried out daily between 9am and 5:30pm. Out of 1,800 targeted registered voters aged 18 and above drawn from the 2022 IEBC register, 1,507 completed interviews, giving an 83.7 percent response rate and a reported margin of error of plus or minus 2.5 percentage points at a 95 percent confidence level.

Early polls measure current name recognition rather than guaranteed Election Day turnout, especially before party primaries test rival coalitions and the Election Campaign Financing Act, 2013, shapes disclosure requirements for county contenders. The next meaningful tests of Tana River's race will be updated voter-register figures from the IEBC, formal candidate clearances, and independent surveys capturing post-2022 voters across all three constituencies.

items.description: The Kariobangi Centre of Excellence, MSEA's model manufacturing and incubation hub, continues to advance grassroots enterprise development through access to productive infrastructure.
content: The Kariobangi Centre of Excellence, MSEA’s model manufacturing and incubation hub, continues to advance grassroots enterprise development through access to productive infrastructure. Today, the Centre hosted an economic empowerment forum during which 44 registered youth and women groups from Mathare Constituency received Common User Machines to strengthen their enterprise operations and productivity.

The forum was presided over by the Principal Secretary, State Department for MSMEs, Hon. Susan Auma Mang’eni, alongside Mathare Constituency MP, Hon. Tom Aluoch, MSEA Board Chairman, Dr. James Mureu, Board Members and Director General/CEO, Mr. Henry Rithaa, bringing together over 600 Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs), including members of registered groups and associations.

In her address, the PS underscored the critical role of MSEs in Kenya’s economy, noting that they account for approximately 98% of businesses in the country. She highlighted the Government’s commitment to expanding economic opportunities for youth through programmes such as the National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA), whose second phase is expected to extend support to more young entrepreneurse across the country.

She also encouraged MSEs to leverage the Kenya Jobs and Economic Transformation (KJET) Project, which strengthens MSME clusters through capacity building and co-investment support along priority value chains. Additionally, she sensitised participants on the ongoing AGPO training programme, accessible through *254#, which equips participants with the knowledge and certification needed to access government procurement opportunities. She urged youth and women to take advantage of the programme and explore available financing opportunities through the Hustler Fund, Uwezo Fund, Women Enterprise Fund and Youth Enterprise Development Fund.

Speaking during the forum, MSEA Director General/CEO, Mr. Henry Rithaa, encouraged the beneficiary groups to make productive use of the equipment, noting that access to appropriate machinery is essential in strengthening enterprise capacity, improving productivity and creating employment opportunities. He further emphasised the importance of organised groups in leveraging shared infrastructure to grow sustainable businesses.

The 44 beneficiary groups received a range of equipment, including car wash machines, welding machines, sewing machines, generators and woodworking machines. The equipment will support various enterprise activities, enhance production capabilities and open up additional income-generating opportunities for youth and women within Mathare Constituency.

Through Centres of Excellence and enterprise development programmes, MSEA continues to bring productive infrastructure, business support and economic opportunities closer to MSEs, advancing inclusive growth, job creation and the development of a competitive MSE sector.
Present at the forum were representatives from Uwezo Fund, Women Enterprise Fund, the National Government Administration and other stakeholders.

The Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) has announced a two-month closure of the Lower Kabete-Ndumbuini/Kapenguria Road-Uthiru Interchange to allow contractors to carry out reconstruction of the interchange's ramps, loops, and slip roads.
In a public notice dated Wednesday, November 25, KeNHA confirmed the closure will take effect on Wednesday, December 2, 2026, and remain in force until Sunday, January 31, 2027.
Motorists on the Nairobi-Nakuru Highway corridor are advised to use designated alternative routes for the duration of the works.

KeNHA Director GeneralLuka Kimeli called on road users to adhere to the temporary traffic management plan, follow all posted road signs, and cooperate with police officers and traffic marshals deployed at the site.

Drivers heading from Nairobi along the A8 (Waiyaki Way) towards Ndumbuini have three options available to them.

The first requires exiting at Kabete Technical, proceeding to the Naivasha Road roundabout, using the Uthiru Underpass, and then rejoining the Nairobi-bound carriageway before taking Marigoini Cabro Road to Ndumbuini Shopping Centre.

The third route involves continuing to the 87/Muhuri Interchange, situated past Shell Kinoo, and using the 87-Ndumbuini Road near 87 Mall.
Motorists coming from Rironi or Nakuru who need to reach Ndumbuini will be required to turn at the Muhuri Interchange and proceed along the Muhuri-Ndumbuini Road.

Motorists from Uthiru and Kawangware have been directed to conduct all turning manoeuvres to and from Naivasha Road through either the Uthiru Underpass or the Muhuri Interchange.
KeNHA has released a traffic management map detailing the affected sections, road closures, and alternative routes.
The authority urged motorists to study the alternative routes in advance of travel and to heed instructions from traffic officers and marshals stationed along the diversion corridors.

The hoisting operations were scheduled for Saturday and Sunday nights, November 21 and 22, 2026, between 11:00 p.m. and 4:00 a.m.
Motorists travelling between Nairobi and Thika were advised to use alternative routes via the Shell Petrol Station to rejoin the highway during the closures.

The poll placed Dado at 53 percent support among respondents asked whom they would back if the election were held today, more than four times the share recorded by second-placed Said Hiribae at 12.9 percent. Still, 22.6 percent of respondents said they remained undecided, leaving a substantial swing bloc unaligned more than 20 months before polling day.

Behind Dado and Hiribae, the remaining field polled in single digits in Mizani Africa's snapshot. Nuh Nassir drew 7.3 percent support, followed by Hero Said at 2.3 percent and Hassan Morowa at 1.9 percent, pointing to heavy early consolidation behind the former county chief alongside deep voter hesitation.

Kenya's county governors are elected by simple plurality under Article 180 of the Constitution, running alongside a nominated deputy governor rather than facing a 50-percent runoff threshold. In Mizani Africa's snapshot, the four trailing contenders combined drew 24.4 percent, meaning Dado's 53 percent score exceeds all named rivals and the 22.6 percent undecided group individually, though coalition realignments and undecided turnout still leave the contest fluid.

Under Article 180(7) of the Constitution of Kenya, county governors are barred from holding office for more than two consecutive terms, turning the 2027 contest into an open succession race whenever a two-term incumbent steps aside. In an open field, early name recognition often favours a former governor such as Dado before party nominations and coalition alignments settle the final ballot.

Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) 2022 county data underline how concentrated Tana River's electorate is compared with larger urban counties. Of Kenya's 22,102,532 registered county voters in 2022, Tana River accounted for 141,096 voters across three constituencies: Garsen with 55,453 (39.3 percent of the county total), Bura with 45,678 (32.4 percent), and Galole with 39,965 (28.3 percent).

Within the six Coast counties, IEBC 2022 records show Tana River holds the second-smallest electorate, trailing Mombasa (641,913), Kilifi (588,602), Kwale (328,253), and Taita Taveta (181,827), and standing ahead of only Lamu (81,453). Because total county registration sits near 141,000 voters, modest shifts in turnout or local endorsements across Garsen, Bura, and Galole can swing final margins faster than in populous coastal cities.

Those constituency weights mean a candidate who wins decisive backing in Garsen and Bura can build a commanding county-wide lead even before Galole breaks. Conversely, with 22.6 percent of polled voters undecided, a coordinated shift across any single constituency or late coalition endorsement could alter the gap markedly once formal campaigns begin.

Mizani Africa conducted fieldwork between November 2 and November 12, 2026, using mobile telephone interviews carried out daily between 9am and 5:30pm. Out of 1,800 targeted registered voters aged 18 and above drawn from the 2022 IEBC register, 1,507 completed interviews, giving an 83.7 percent response rate and a reported margin of error of plus or minus 2.5 percentage points at a 95 percent confidence level.

Early polls measure current name recognition rather than guaranteed Election Day turnout, especially before party primaries test rival coalitions and the Election Campaign Financing Act, 2013, shapes disclosure requirements for county contenders. The next meaningful tests of Tana River's race will be updated voter-register figures from the IEBC, formal candidate clearances, and independent surveys capturing post-2022 voters across all three constituencies.

items.title: Sports Department Warns Sh8.38 Billion Budget Shortfall Could Jeopardise AFCON 2027 Preparations
items.description: Kenya's AFCON 2027 preparations face a potential funding challenge after the Sports Department disclosed an Sh8.38 billion recurrent budget shortfall.
content: State Department for Sports says it needs Sh10.78 billion in recurrent funding but has received only Sh2.39 billion as Kenya prepares for major international sporting competitions.
Newsroom · lets crawlers and assistive tech read the precise publication time while readers see a stable date with the year. --> 25 November 2026 · 3 min read

Kenya’s preparations to host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) and the 2028 World Athletics Championships could face financial challenges after the State Department for Sports revealed an Sh8.38 billion funding shortfall in its proposed 2027/2028 budget.
Principal Secretary Elijah Mwangi raised the concern before the National Assembly Sports and Culture Committee, chaired by Dan Wanyama, while presenting the department’s budget proposals.

Mwangi said the department requires Sh10.78 billion to meet its recurrent expenditure obligations in the 2027/2028 financial year but has been allocated only Sh2.39 billion under the Budget Policy Statement (BPS).
The allocation leaves a deficit of Sh8.38 billion, which the PS warned could undermine the department’s ability to implement critical programmes and meet its financial obligations.
Mwangi attributed the increased budgetary requirements partly to preparations for hosting major international sporting competitions.
According to the PS, AFCON 2027 preparations require Sh3.55 billion, while preparations for the 2029 World Athletics Championships require approximately Sh3.9 billion.
He told MPs that the proposed funding would also cater for essential recurrent expenses needed to sustain departmental operations and deliver its core programmes.
“The higher requirement in FY 2027/28 are for preparation to host AFCON 2027 which is Sh3,546,789,165 and the 2029 World Athletics Championships which is Sh3.9 billion,” Mwangi told the committee.

The department's total resource requirement for the 2027/2028 financial year stands at Sh42.01 billion, comprising Sh10.78 billion for recurrent expenditure and Sh31.23 billion for development programmes.
However, the Budget Policy Statement provides an allocation of Sh27.75 billion, leaving the department with an overall funding gap of approximately Sh14.26 billion.

The shortfall raises questions about the government's financial preparedness to deliver the infrastructure, logistics and administrative requirements associated with hosting major international sporting events.

During the committee proceedings, Wanyama urged the department to ensure that available resources are fairly distributed, particularly in settling outstanding debts owed to sports federations and other creditors.
He also called for the completion of sports academies being established across constituencies, noting the importance of investing in grassroots talent development.

The committee chairperson observed that funding national teams remained one of the primary responsibilities of the Sports Fund but expressed concern over the financial difficulties facing several federations.

“The issue of funding of national team was one of the priority things that the sports fund must do. So far we are doing well but federations have issues that you have quite a number of debts to pay to them and they are having a lot of problems,” Wanyama said.

Meanwhile, the State Department for Youth Affairs and Creative Economy, led by Principal Secretary Jacob Fikirini, raised concerns over the lack of funding for film location mapping in the 2027/2028 financial year.
Fikirini told MPs that the project remained ongoing and was expected to be completed by June 2027.

The department further reported receiving a recurrent allocation of Sh974.95 million in the current financial year, against expenditure of Sh400.99 million, representing an absorption rate of 41 percent.

Separately, Principal Secretary Ummi Bashir of the State Department for Culture, Arts and Heritage asked the committee to recommend additional funding to support departmental programmes and responsibilities.

The department cited inadequate funding for key priorities among its semi-autonomous government agencies, including the National Lottery Board, Kenya National Library Service and National Heroes Council.
It said additional resources were necessary to enable the institutions to implement planned activities and fulfil their respective mandates.

items.description: PSG have the chance to remain atop the Champions League table when they host AS Roma in the headline fixture on Wednesday night.
content: PSG have the chance to remain atop the Champions League table when they host AS Roma in the headline fixture on Wednesday night.
The back-to-back Champions League winners are unbeaten and have 12 points from their opening four games.
Barcelona, Liverpool and Sporting Lisbon are also all in action on Wednesday, looking to record positive results to remain in the top 10 position in the league phase.
With another nine matches scheduled to be played, we have a look at the top games and offer our predicted outcomes.
ALSO READ: UEFA Champions League round five predictions: Tuesday match previews, key stats, current form & h2h
The hosts are in 31st place with three points ahead of the crucial match, knowing that defeat will definitely relegate them from the competition.
They have an uphill task against fifth place Barcelona who are seeking a fifth consecutive victory in all competitions.
Barca are coming off an impressive 3-2 comeback victory against Villarreal over the weekend, while Sabah were 2-0 winners against Kapaz in the Azerbaijan league.
Raphinha has scored six goals in his last four Champions League appearances and has 23 goals in his last 26 appearances in the competition.
The Brazilian and Lamine Yamal will be the main attacking outlets for the visiting team, who are tipped as favorites to win convincingly.
Prediction – Barcelona to win + Over 2.5 goals
This match pits two sides against each other with nothing to separate them in the Champions League this season.
Both teams come into the game with nine points and a similar goal difference (4) as they look to cement a qualification place.
The home team are in better form, unbeaten in their last 11 matches, confident they can get a positive result against the reds.
Liverpool will be boosted by their emphatic 4-0 win against Manchester United over the weekend.
Liverpool have scored 14 goals and conceded 10 in their first four league-phase games.
The 10 goals conceded are already their highest total after four Champions League group-stage/league-phase matches in club history.
The hosts have been poor in the Champions League and only have one point after four matches.
They face a 13th place Bayern Munich who have eight points as they seek to break into the top eight positions.
Lille have lost both games they have played against Bayern by a 7-1 aggregate scoreline back in 2012.
Bayern have scored at least twice in 12 of their last 13 Champions League matches.
Their last 10 Champions League games have produced 50 goals — exactly five per match on average.
Lille have also scored in their last nine Champions League home matches, and every one of those games has featured a first-half goal.
The holders have been supreme in the competition and are at the top of the standings with 12 points after a perfect start to the campaign.
Paris are unbeaten in their last 14 Champions League matches, winning 10 and drawing four.
That is a club record and equals Lyon’s French record for consecutive unbeaten matches in the competition.
PSG have scored 20 goals in their first four league-phase games, the highest total of any team at this stage. They also bring a 12-game winning streak to the game.
Roma have won only one of their last 11 Champions League away matches, while they have conceded in their last 33 away matches in the competition.
The home team are seeking a sixth straight win in all competitions when they host a struggling Man United on Wednesday.
Sporting have won their last five matches in all competitions and victory here will see them cement their qualification hopes.
United, who appointed Mauricio Pochettino, as their new manager suffered an embarrassing 4-0 defeat away at Liverpool over the weekend and are desperate for a positive result here.
The Red Devils are in 17th place with six points and must avoid defeat to keep any qualification hopes alive.
The last time these sides met was in the 2007 Champions League and United won both legs with a 3-1 aggregate score.
Prediction – Sporting to win or draw (1X)

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier Arrives in Kenya for an Official Visit
items.description: German President Frank-Walter in Kenya for an official visit expected to strengthen cooperation between the Kenya and Germany.
content: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has arrived in Kenya for an official visit expected to strengthen cooperation between the two countries and create new opportunities in trade, investment, education, and technology.

Steinmeier arrived in Nairobi on Tuesday night, November 24, and was received at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport by Prime Cabinet Secretary and Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs Musalia Mudavadi.

He is accompanied by a German business delegation and is set to hold bilateral talks with President William Ruto at State House aimed at advancing their common goals and opening up new possibilities for mutually beneficial cooperation.

The discussions are expected to focus on trade and investment, clean energy, climate action, education, technology and skills development.

In a statement following his arrival, Mudavadi said the visit provides an opportunity for Kenya and Germany to strengthen their longstanding partnership and explore new areas of cooperation and share a vision for sustainable development.
“Kenya and Germany share a longstanding partnership built on mutual trust, economic cooperation and a common vision for sustainable development,” he said.

He pointed out that increased investment, job and training possibilities for young Kenyans, and the sharing of technology and information could all be facilitated by closer relations between the two nations.
According to Mudavadi, “strengthening these ties can unlock greater investment, expand employment and training opportunities for young Kenyans, and facilitate knowledge and technology exchange.”
The visit will also include engagements with Kenya-Germany cooperation projects in healthcare, digital services, skills development, arts and culture, as well as nature and biodiversity conservation.
The visit is expected to provide an opportunity for both countries to strengthen their relationship and identify new ways of working together for mutual benefit.

items.title: Central Papua HIV Treatment Reaches Just 21.5% of Diagnosed Residents
items.description: Central Papua health data through September 2026 show only 4,209 of 19,564 diagnosed residents living with HIV receive daily antiretroviral therapy.
content: Central Papua health data through September 2026 show only 4,209 of 19,564 diagnosed residents living with HIV receive daily antiretroviral therapy.

Nearly four in five people diagnosed with HIV in Indonesia's Central Papua province are not receiving antiretroviral medication, provincial health officials disclosed on Wednesday, exposing a stark gap between case detection and sustained treatment across the remote highlands.

Speaking in the provincial capital of Nabire, Isak Waine, head of communicable disease prevention and control at the Central Papua Provincial Health Office, said program records through September 2026 counted 19,564 living residents who know their HIV-positive status. Only 4,209 of them, or 21.5% based on the province's published figures, were recorded as receiving antiretroviral therapy, leaving 15,355 diagnosed residents outside active treatment.

Provincial surveillance data show that drop-offs continue after patients begin medication. Among the 4,209 residents on antiretroviral drugs, 1,360 had undergone viral load testing through September 2026, representing 32.3% of treated patients, and 1,191 had achieved viral suppression.

Those figures carry a sharp split in clinical outcomes. While 87.6% of tested patients suppressed the virus to levels low enough to block sexual transmission under the Undetectable equals Untransmittable principle, they account for only 28.3% of people on medication and just 6.1% of all 19,564 diagnosed residents.

Central Papua's 21.5% treatment rate sits more than 45 percentage points below Indonesia's national treatment coverage. A June 2026 rapid risk assessment by Indonesia's Ministry of Health estimated 557,000 people living with HIV nationwide, with 71%, or 275,942 people, knowing their status and 75% of newly identified cases in the first half of 2026 starting antiretroviral therapy.

In an earlier June 2025 briefing on its 2030 HIV elimination target, the Ministry of Health reported that 67% of diagnosed residents nationwide were on antiretroviral treatment and 55% had reached viral suppression. Officials there classified Central Papua among 11 priority provinces holding 76% of Indonesia's cases and warned that, unlike elsewhere in Indonesia, transmission in Papua had reached the general population at an estimated 2.3% prevalence.

The national briefing also found that while HIV elsewhere in Indonesia remains concentrated in key populations such as sex workers and people who inject drugs, transmission in Papua has already spread into the general population. That broader epidemiological profile makes treatment interruptions far harder to contain across remote regencies.

Ministry of Health figures show why Central Papua remains a national priority. Indonesia ranks 14th globally in total people living with HIV and ninth in new infections, and infectious disease director Ina Agustina warned in June 2025 that rising sexually transmitted infections, including 23,347 syphilis cases and 10,506 gonorrhoea cases recorded the previous year, open further pathways for HIV transmission among working-age adults aged 25 to 49.

Across Central Papua, provincial authorities say strengthening service delivery inside hospitals and community health centres known as puskesmas is critical to keeping patients in care. Waine said the drive forms part of Governor Meki Nawipa and Deputy Governor Deinas Geley's health agenda covering HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria, while urging residents not to let fear or social stigma block early therapy. Waine also emphasised that the health office's goal extends beyond case detection: "Our target is not only finding new cases, but ensuring every person diagnosed with HIV receives ARV treatment, adheres to medication, and achieves suppressed viral load."

Waine said the health office is prioritising closer accompaniment immediately after diagnosis so residents start medication without delay. "Do not be afraid, do not be ashamed, and do not give up. HIV is not the end of life," he said, adding that regular therapy and viral load testing allow people living with HIV to "live healthy, productive lives, work, marry, and build families."

Because Central Papua's September report covers only diagnosed residents who are alive and registered in health records, it does not measure undiagnosed infections across highland districts. Closing the gap toward Indonesia's 2030 elimination goals will depend on expanding viral-load laboratory reach and sustaining monthly drug supply across regional hospitals and community health centres.

items.title: Zambia HIV Agency Warns Donor Cuts Threaten Treatment Gains
items.description: Zambia's National AIDS Council warns shrinking donor funding threatens its 98-98-97 HIV gains after UNAIDS data showed PrEP uptake fell by half.
content: Zambia's National AIDS Council warns shrinking donor funding threatens its 98-98-97 HIV gains after UNAIDS data showed PrEP uptake fell by half.

Zambia's National HIV/AIDS/STI/TB Council (NAC) urged health authorities and international partners on November 25, 2026, to safeguard equitable access to HIV prevention, testing, and treatment, warning that shrinking foreign donor support threatens decades of public health progress.

NAC Director General Dr. Kebby Musokotwane issued the warning ahead of World AIDS Day on December 1 under the global theme "Ending AIDS Starts With Access," one day after UNAIDS reported that pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake in Zambia fell by more than half between 2024 and 2025.

On treatment metrics, Zambia remains one of the strongest performers globally. Ministry of Health and NAC figures show the country has surpassed the UNAIDS 95-95-95 adult benchmarks, reaching 98-98-97: 98 percent of people living with HIV know their status, 98 percent of those diagnosed receive antiretroviral therapy, and 97 percent on treatment achieve viral suppression. UNAIDS estimates also show new infections fell 52 percent between 2010 and 2025.

Yet prevention data reveal a sharp divergence beneath that headline success. According to Ministry of Health figures cited during national prevention planning, Zambia recorded roughly 30,000 new HIV infections in 2024, up from 23,000 in 2023. Adolescents and young people aged 15 to 24 accounted for 38 percent of new cases, with adolescent girls and young women facing three times the risk of male peers.

Zambia's vulnerability stems heavily from how its HIV response has been financed. A peer-reviewed modeling analysis co-authored by Musokotwane and published in the Annals of Internal Medicine noted that the United States President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) supplied 84 percent of Zambia's HIV program funding at the start of 2025, making the country acutely exposed to bilateral aid disruptions.

Global financing data released by UNAIDS on November 24 underscore the scale of that shock. Across low- and middle-income countries, international HIV resources dropped by more than $1 billion in 2025, leaving a $4.3 billion annual shortfall against what is required to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030. In Zambia, Cameroon, and Nigeria, PrEP delivery dropped by over 50 percent.

Bilateral replacement funding has also stalled. According to Health Policy Watch, Zambia postponed signing a proposed multiyear United States health aid memorandum of understanding in late 2025 and requested revisions in February 2026 after Washington linked the billion-dollar package to access to Zambian minerals, including copper and cobalt.

Musokotwane told local media on November 25 that service access remains the dividing line between life and death, particularly for low-income households, young people, and rural residents who face long travel distances to clinics. Earlier Zambian warnings at the June 2026 United Nations High-Level Meeting on HIV/AIDS cautioned that funding gaps risk drug resistance, premature deaths, and lost productivity.

UNAIDS data indicate that community-led clinics have absorbed the sharpest blow from financing cuts. A 2026 UNAIDS survey of 79 community organizations across 47 countries documented a 50 percent drop in PrEP provision, alongside an 85 percent decline in services for gay and bisexual men and an 82 percent drop for sex workers. In Zambia, the Civil Society Self-Coordinating Mechanism has urged Lusaka to adopt a national social contracting policy so community groups can maintain outreach as foreign grants recede.

To close the prevention gap, Zambia launched twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir in December 2025 alongside its 2025-2030 HIV Prevention Roadmap, which aims to halve annual new infections to 15,000 by 2030, and introduced the dapivirine vaginal ring in April 2026. The strategy relies on integrating HIV services into primary healthcare and tapping domestic budgets, including the Constituency Development Fund, to offset donor cuts.

Yet rolling out long-acting prevention products requires sustained procurement budgets and clinic staffing at the exact moment external grants are contracting. Whether Zambia can protect its 98-98-97 treatment gains while reversing the 2024-2025 drop in PrEP coverage will depend on domestic budget allocations and any revised donor agreements ahead of World AIDS Day.
